title: Microsoft Viva: identifiable export of Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents administrator-controlled identifiable exports, the licensing prerequisite and the policy controls. Minor corrections remain for omitted navigation headings, an uncited PowerShell reference and checklist controls missing from the table; the documentation still describes preview behaviour while the roadmap reports In development.

claims.quote: Microsoft Viva: Copilot Analytics - Identifiable Export metrics in the Copilot Dashboard

claims.claim: The roadmap describes exporting identifiable row-level Copilot metrics for reporting and deeper analysis.
claims.quote: This enables users to export Identifiable row-level Copilot metrics from the Copilot Dashboard for reporting and deeper analysis.

claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators can turn the capability on in a tenant.
claims.quote: This capability can be tuned On by Admins in a tenant.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.

claims.claim: Identification access is enabled through Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > On.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select Create a policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].ui.path and its rendered path to 'Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > On'. The initial Settings heading is omitted; the remaining printed steps are supported.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <featureId> -Name <policyName> -IsFeatureEnabled $true -Everyone enables the selected identification feature tenant-wide.
claims.quote: The IsFeatureEnabled parameter specifies whether or not the feature is enabled by the policy. Valid values are: - $true: The feature is enabled by the policy. - $false: The feature is not enabled by the policy.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchange/add-vivamodulefeaturepolicy?view=exchange-ps to sources; it explicitly documents the printed parameters and Boolean values. Neither printed call needs to change.

claims.claim: The existing export policy is disabled through Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > Off.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select Create a policy. ... Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].ui.path and its rendered path to 'Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting > Off'. The initial Settings heading is omitted; the remaining printed steps are supported.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId <featureId> -Name <policyName> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone disables the selected export feature tenant-wide, subject to the documented analyst exception.
claims.quote: The policy disables the feature for the specified users and group members. If you want to disable the feature for all users, use the -Everyone parameter instead.

claims.claim: Learn does not print a feature ID specifically for identifiable Copilot Dashboard export.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Dashboard identifiable feature ID default; Copilot Dashboard identifiable export default IdentifiableExport feature ID pricing license. claims.claim: Replacing -Everyone with -GroupIds or -UserIds scopes a policy to selected groups or users.
claims.quote: This example adds a policy for the Reflection feature in Viva Insights. The policy disables the feature for the specified users and group members. If you want to disable the feature for all users, use the -Everyone parameter instead.

claims.claim: User-level export and insights is always on for analysts and cannot be changed for that role.
claims.quote: Since analysts already have access to user-level data through advanced analysis experiences, the above-mentioned setting is always on for the analyst role and can't be changed.

claims.claim: A single unified VFAM export control governs both week-level and day-level exports.

claims.claim: Each feature permits up to 10 policies assigned to users and groups.

claims.claim: Each user/group policy can cover at most 20 users or groups.

claims.quote: You can assign one additional policy per feature to the entire tenant by using the -Everyone parameter, which will function as a global default state for that feature across your organization.
